contracts.rule: A concept image never gets a node in the task graph: `generateConcept` records a hash of the request (prompt, params, refs) as the asset's `sourceTask`, and nothing a run plans consumes the asset, so a project holding a concept plans exactly the tasks it planned before.
contracts.prevents: A concept bound to `{locationId: 'cafe'}` being taken for that location's plate, or a sketch the author asked for changing what the next run plans and pays for.
contracts.detail: The asset is bound to what it sketches so the document tree and the backlink panel can find it. Every binding lookup outside the document tree filters by `kind` first, and the planner resolves a shot's plate by task hash rather than by manifest binding.

contracts.rule: A shot's task inputs carry its location twice: `buildShotPrompt` names the location, and the plate's asset hash leads `refs`. So rewriting a scene's heading re-keys every shot in the scene, unlike retyping a line, which re-keys nothing.
contracts.prevents: Treating a heading edit as free, like other prose edits, when the next run re-renders every shot in the scene; the price has to be shown before the edit runs.
contracts.detail: The planner passes the plate first in `upstream`, then each subject's portrait and outfit sheet. A heading edit inverts the rule that prose edits are reported as drift rather than re-rendered, so the price counts these shots as `restaged`, never as `drifted` (`script.headingRestagesShots`, in `@vn/scriptedit`).

contracts.rule: `solve` enumerates a family's slots whether or not anything has been drawn, and attaches a task hash only to a slot whose kind can resolve its inputs now; any other slot carries the kind's sentence saying why. Edges come from each kind's `refs`, never from `Task.deps`.
contracts.prevents: A graph of task hashes cannot show work not yet planned, because a downstream hash embeds its upstream outputs, so every surface would have to guess at it.
contracts.detail: The first enumeration of an address wins and later ones are dropped. `Solution.order` is upstream first, and a walk that meets a reference cycle already on disk stops rather than hanging. A ref to an address with no slot is an opaque upstream, such as an authored pin. `Task.deps` is incomplete and is not hashed, so edges are never derived from it. Each slot kind that carries this contract adds its `slot:` prefix to the subjects in the index.

contracts.rule: A shot in a staging-sheet group carries `params.extra.sheet`, a hash of the sheet's prompt, its reference hashes in order and the group seed, so anything the sheet is drawn from re-keys every member at once. A shot in no group carries no `extra`.
contracts.prevents: A member drawn from an old sheet while the others are cut from a new one, or a sheet change that re-renders nothing, because the sheet's inputs are not in any member's identity.
contracts.detail: What re-keys the members: the members and their order, each member's framing, cast and camera, the plate, and the group's notes and seed. A shot outside a group carries no `extra`, so no hash that predates the field moved. The seeds are derived from the project and the manifest, never from a task graph, by `sheetSeeds`, which the planner, the scheduled runner and `gengraph.run` all call; a group's seed and notes live in the shots file and reach the model's production map beside the members. A sheet is rerolled by changing its seed (`story.setSheetGroup`), never by force: `gengraph.run` refuses `force` on a graph where a node feeds more than one output (`sharedAncestors`), because a forced run to one output would redraw the sheet for it alone and leave the other members' frames cut from the old one with nothing to re-key them. Every slot a graph binds shares its one journal and its one `Graph` object in a process, and `runBoundGraph` serialises the runs of one graph, because seeds are written onto the graph's own sockets: two members running at once would read each other's prompt and references, and the sheet would be drawn once per member rather than once per group.

contracts.rule: A task is identified by `sha256(kind, inputs)`, where the inputs are the normalized prompt, the ordered reference asset hashes and the params, and never the model id. Identical work therefore collapses to one node.
contracts.prevents: Changing `models.image` re-keying every task, so that every drawn slot is drawn again, or two requests for the same picture each paying for it.
contracts.detail: The model id is left out so that changing `models.image` in `project.yaml` does not re-key every task: a rendered slot keeps its picture, and the new model is used for slots not yet drawn, for a regenerate, and where a slot's own `model` override names it. `taskHash` removes `modelId` from the inputs and from their `params` before hashing. A node that has not drawn yet (`pending` or `failed`) takes the inputs of the latest planning pass in `TaskGraph.add`, so it follows the project's current model; a `done` or `needs_human` node keeps the inputs it ran with. The asset records the model that drew it (`Asset.modelId`, always the author's spelling, never OpenRouter's) and, optionally, the key that carried the call (`Asset.transport`). A picture drawn through OpenRouter has the same identity as one drawn natively, so adding a vendor's key later redraws nothing. `params` is `image_params` with the narrowest authored seed applied (`seedFor`) and, for a shot, its own `aspect` in place of the project's (`aspectFor`). Both return the project's params by identity when nothing was authored, so a project that authored neither hashes as it did before either field existed. The model id is resolved the same way (`modelFor`: the narrowest `imageModel` rung, else `models.image`) but, being outside the hash, changes nothing about identity. Because identical work collapses to one node, dedupe, resumability and staleness come at no extra cost: `TaskGraph.add` answers the existing node for a known hash and adds any new dependency edges to it. `packages/pipeline/src/tests/prompthash.test.ts` guards the hashes of a real project against a committed baseline that is never regenerated; this rule's pinning test checks `taskHash` and `TaskGraph.add` directly.
